subject: Flexible Commit Scenarios for Q4 runway

Date: Mon, 10 Aug 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Exploring commit options for next 12 months

Hi Lauren,

We loved the demo last week — the latency on batch reranking was impressive. Our analytics engine will start shifting production inference to hosted endpoints in Q4. Before we move forward we need clarity on pricing and commitment flexibility.

High level of what we need: 
- 12 month horizon but we may want to convert to quarterly cadence after the first 3 months
- A starter path for POC traffic (~10M tokens/month), growth path if usage doubles, and an enterprise option for sustained 500M+/mo in year two
- Questions: are there carryover tokens if we underuse a month? Can we do partial quarterly true-ups instead of annual true-up? How are overage rates calculated?

Can you share a couple of concrete commit scenarios (token tiers + per-token effective pricing) and the limitations around contract changes mid-term?

Thanks,
Dana Lopez
Head of Platform, Acme Analytics
Dana.Lopez@acme-analytics.com

From: lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwoodinference.com>

Subject: Re: Exploring commit options for next 12 months

Dana — thanks for the clear summary and great to hear the demo resonated. I attached a short worksheet (pricing_worksheet_v1.xlsx) with three starter scenarios and the math behind the effective per-1M-token price. High-level options below:

1) Starter (POC-friendly) — 12 month, 120M token annual commit (10M/mo average)
   - Baseline: $18.00 / 1M tokens hosted API list rate
   - Commit price: $14.40 / 1M (20% discount)
   - Overages: billed at $16.20 / 1M (10% discount to list)
   - Carryover: up to 20% of monthly shortfall can roll month-to-month, expires quarterly

2) Growth — 12 month, 720M token annual commit (avg 60M/mo)
   - Commit price: $11.70 / 1M (35% discount)
   - Overages: $13.50 / 1M
   - Quarterly true-up allowed; one mid-term downscale (<=20% reduction) with 30-day notice

3) Enterprise — 12 month, 6B token annual commit (sustained high volume)
   - Commit price: $8.50 / 1M (53% discount)
   - Overages: $9.90 / 1M
   - Carryover: full unused tokens carry across the year (no expiry)
   - Includes 99.9% SLA, private telemetry feed, and extended retention controls (add-on)

Notes and trade-offs:
- We price based on 1M-token units and bill monthly against committed allocation.
- Carryover policies are stricter at Starter level to limit credit exposure.
- We allow one contract amendment in first 90 days for Growth/Enterprise but it is subject to repricing.
- Doc: see attached worksheet for line-item math and example month-by-month scenarios.

If you want, we can sketch a hybrid (quarterly commits that ladder up to an annual bucket) — that usually helps customers balance runway with budget approvals. If you confirm which scenario is closest we’ll run legal/pricing checks and scope any SLA add-ons.

Best,
Lauren Bishop

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
To: lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwoodinference.com>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 11 Aug 2026 09:20:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Exploring commit options for next 12 months

Lauren/Marissa — quick internal note on margins and guardrails before we go back with concessions:

- Starter: 20% discount with 10% overage keeps unit economics acceptable for POC. Approve as-is.
- Growth: 35% discount is aggressive but ok if we require quarterly true-ups and limit one downscale <=20% in year 1. Add a 6% early-termination fee pro-rated on committed tokens to discourage churn.
- Enterprise: 53% is doable only for multi-year lock or a stronger consumption profile; recommend we require a 12-month minimum plus an optional 6-month notice for downscale.

Operational asks if we grant carryover: enforce expiration windows and cap on monthly rolled amount (e.g., no more than 50% of monthly committed allocation can be retroactively used). Also recommend we keep overage price at minimum 10% above commit price to manage burst risk.

If we need to give more flexibility for procurement, suggest we trade on SLA and telemetry features rather than deeper per-token cuts.

Rishi
Head of Revenue Operations
From: Dana Lopez <dana.lopez@acme-analytics.com>
To: lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@acme-analytics.com>
Date: Tue, 11 Aug 2026 16:00:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Flexible Commit Scenarios for Q4 runway

Hi Lauren — thanks for the clear scenarios. A few follow-ups from procurement and finance: 

1) Quarterly commits: we prefer quarterly commit windows (for budgetary visibility) with an annual floor rather than a strict annual prepayment. Is a laddered quarterly model possible where each quarter is committed but contributes to an annual bucket?
2) Carryover: the Starter carryover expiring quarterly is acceptable, but Procurement wants a 3-month lookback for usage smoothing (i.e., unused tokens in month n can be used for n+1 and n+2).
3) Overage protection: can we have a capped overage rate (e.g., no more than 150% of commit price) for any month to avoid bill shock during sudden spikes?
4) Contract changes: if we move to quarterly commits, what happens to the Enterprise SLA add-ons pricing?

We are leaning toward a Growth path but would like the quarterly-ladder + capped overage protection. Also attach a short procurement questionnaire — can you confirm SOC2 scope and data residency options?

Thanks,
Dana

Dana — appreciate the follow-ups and the procurement questionnaire (we have a SOC 2 Type II report, and data residency options across us-west and eu-west — I’ve noted your preference for US residency in the procurement doc and will confirm tenancy options).

Quick answers and a path forward: 
- Quarterly-ladder model: yes, we can do quarterly commits that ladder into an annual floor. Proposal: customer signs a 12-month agreement with quarterly committed amounts (Q1..Q4) that must sum to >= 60% of the annual floor. Quarterly true-ups reconcile usage to committed amounts. This preserves predictable revenue while giving budget visibility.
- Carryover: Accept Procurement’s 3-month lookback for Starter (unused tokens can be applied to the next two months after their origin month, and to the quarter true-up). We’ll cap retroactive usage at 50% of a given month’s committed allocation to limit credit risk.
- Overage cap: We can agree to a capped overage exposure of 150% of the commit price per month. Practically that maps to: monthly overage per-1M <= 1.5 * (commit price / 1M). This prevents bill shock.
- SLA & quarterly commits: SLA add-ons (99.9%) remain available under quarterly model; pricing for telemetry and retention controls is additive and will be listed separately in the MSA.

Concessions approved by Revenue Ops (cc: Rishi): Starter carryover 3-month lookback, quarterly-ladder allowed with annual floor >= 60%, overage cap 150% of commit price. Growth/Enterprise policy unchanged except we’ll allow quarterly commits to ladder if the annual floor and minimum notice windows are preserved.

Next steps: I’ll update the worksheet with the quarterly-ladder math, attach a draft MSA (redwood_msa_draft.pdf) and a DocuSign link. If Procurement is happy with SOC2 scope and residency, we can send the DocuSign and schedule a 30-minute signature & kickoff call.
